content: Dart Sass treats bare min(), max(), and clamp() as Sass built-in functions, not CSS math functions. In Sprockets + Dart Sass, writing width: min(100%, 400px) in a .scss file causes SassError: incompatible units during asset compilation. The project already hit this exact issue in v1.18 (feeds.css.scss: max(100%, min-content) replaced with width: 100%). Fix: wrap in calc() — calc(min(100%, 400px)) is treated as a CSS calc expression and Sass does not recurse into it. Sass 1.40+ handles clamp() as a calculation type, but older versions do not. Documented in sass/sass GitHub issues and CSS-Tricks.
